We visited the New 7 Wonders of the World on 1 ticket — here's how Editor's Note Members of our video team just visited all seven New Wonders of the World — from Machu Picchu in Peru to the Taj Mahal in India — and one special type of plane ticket made it possible. The Oneworld airline alliance offers a Round The World (RTW) ticket that lets you visit (almost) as many countries as you like, all on one itinerary at one price. Check out the full video here — and keep reading to learn how to book your own round-the-world adventure. What is a round-the-world ticket? Oneworld's RTW tickets offer hundreds of destinations in 170 countries and territories, with three types of fares: - Oneworld Explorer: The price you pay depends on the number of continents you visit, with up to 15 flight segments on one ticket. - Global Explorer: The fare depends on the distance you travel, with a total cap of 39,000 miles. However, this includes additional partner airlines like Aer Lingus and WestJet. - Circle Pacific: Only includes continents that border the Pacific Ocean. The cost of a ticket starts around $3,600 for a three-continent journey in economy class. To cover all seven Wonders, two members of our intrepid team took RTW tickets in business class. Between them, they covered six continents and traveled on seven different Oneworld airlines. Maximizing rewards on your ticket Since there's no way to book these tickets with miles, here are our top tips to maximize your rewards on a cash booking. First, you should be able to purchase RTW tickets directly with individual airlines. If you do, make sure you're using a credit card that offers bonus points or miles on airfare purchases. Start by planning your itinerary through Oneworld's site and then call your favorite Oneworld airline (such as American) to book and pay. This way, your transaction will code as an airline purchase, and you'll earn bonus points and any other perks your card might offer. Check out our favorite airline cards for maximizing your RTW ticket purchase. In addition, since these are cash tickets, you'll able to earn miles and credit toward elite status for each flight. Your best option is likely to pick your preferred program — like American AAdvantage or Alaska Atmos Rewards — and add that frequent flyer number to your ticket. Maximizing rewards on your journey Trip expenses don't end after you step off the plane. Our team had to budget for tours and tickets for each of the New Seven Wonders of the World, as well as ground transportation from the airport, and they used the credit cards already in their wallets to help offset these costs. Check your Chase Offers and Amex Offers for targeted savings at tour booking sites like Viator. Or consider redeeming points for tickets through your credit card travel portal. Select American Express cards offer monthly Uber Cash on U.S. Uber rides and Uber Eats orders. Meanwhile, eligible Chase cardholders can unlock bonus points and monthly in-app credits with Lyft. At a minimum, be sure to pay with a card that earns bonus points on general travel to maximize your rewards on tours, tickets and transportation — and make sure you're not paying any pesky foreign transaction fees. Bottom line If you're hoping to book your own round-the-world journey, check out these sample itineraries for inspiration. Alternatively, you can chart your own course with Oneworld's handy tool. Let us know which continents you're dreaming of in the comments!

item.title: Delta cuts 5 routes across 7 cities, plans smaller Las Vegas schedule this winter
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.09
Delta cuts 5 routes across 7 cities, plans smaller Las Vegas schedule this winter As the peak summer travel season wrapped up this past weekend, Delta Air Lines revealed plans to slash five routes from its network. Between now and December, Delta plans to trim a total of three routes from New York City: two from John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and one from LaGuardia Airport (LGA). The Atlanta-based carrier will also end Las Vegas service from two cities in Southern California. It's time to book: When to buy holiday, spring break and summer flights for the best fares in 2026-27 That cutback at Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) came as a result of lower travel demand to Vegas this winter, a spokesperson said. Meanwhile, here's how the airline explained its cuts in New York City: "Delta continually evaluates its network to ensure we're offering a schedule that best meets customer demand," the airline said in a statement about the changes. "We apologize for any inconvenience and will contact impacted customers directly about these changes." Delta's 5 route cuts All five of the routes will end between early November and mid-December. Here's the full rundown of the flights Delta is ending: | Route | End date | |---|---| | LAS to San Diego International Airport (SAN) | Nov. 8 | | LAS to John Wayne Airport (SNA) in Orange County, California | Nov. 8 | | LGA to Tulsa International Airport (TUL) | Nov. 9 | | JFK to Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) | Saturday-only service ends Dec. 19 | | JFK to Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport (MKE) | Dec. 19 | There is a silver lining for Delta flyers in New York and Wisconsin who have taken the JFK-MKE service in the past: The carrier still offers four daily round-trip flights between LGA and MKE. And, Delta does plan to operate some limited Las Vegas service to both San Diego and Orange County in early January. Those flights are meant to cater to travelers attending the city's massive Consumer Electronics Show, where the airline has been a headliner in the past. Cutting back in Las Vegas Delta is not alone in cutting back its Vegas flight schedule. This winter, the airline's total departures from LAS will be down roughly 7% versus last year, according to data from aviation analytics firm Cirium. In 2026, the entire airport is set to see 7% fewer flights than last year, per Cirium. That's after the city as a whole saw a 7.5% dropoff in visitors last year versus 2024, according to the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Bureau. It came amid one of the "more complex operating environments" the tourism sector had seen outside of the COVID-19 pandemic, the organization said in January. Related reading:

item.title: Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.05
Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it? Editor's Note If you fly American Airlines frequently, you may want to consider getting one of its cobranded Citi cards. At the top of the hierarchy is the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees), which offers the most AA-specific perks of any credit card. The card recently underwent a significant refresh in August, which raised the annual fee to $695 but also added substantial new benefits. Doing the math on this card is now more important than ever — but there's also more value to potentially unlock if you maximize each of the new perks. So, is it worth the annual fee — both in year one and beyond? Let's do the math. Welcome bonus New Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard cardholders can currently earn a limited time offer of 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. This bonus is worth about $1,813, based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, and is the highest we've seen on the card, so now is the best time to apply. This bonus accounts for a significant portion of the card's overall value, so earning it and redeeming the miles wisely are crucial to offsetting the card's high annual fee. Related: The Citi / AAdvantage Executive's new benefits are live: 6 things to do now Lounge access Arguably, the most valuable ongoing benefit of this card is the complimentary Admirals Club membership you'll receive every year that you hold it. When you have the Citi / AA Executive, all you have to do is walk to the lounge and present a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight. An annual membership costs $750 to $1,400, depending on your status level and whether you want access only to AA-branded lounges or to partner lounges as well. Given that this card carries a $695 annual fee, it doesn't make sense to buy an Admirals Club membership on its own, unless you aren't eligible for the card. With this card, you'll be able to access almost 50 Admirals Clubs and more than 60 partner lounges worldwide when flying American or one of its Oneworld partners. Notably, this includes Alaska Lounges in hubs like Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Portland International Airport (PDX), San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA). You can bring in either your immediate family members (spouse or domestic partner and children under 18 years of age) or up to two guests. And they don't need to be on the same flight as you — just any American or Oneworld flight with a same-day boarding pass. Related: The best lounge access credit cards to add to your wallet Travel benefits The Citi / AA Executive offers valuable perks when flying American, including priority check-in at business-class counters (where available) and priority boarding privileges (where available) for you and up to eight travelers on the same reservation. You also get your first checked bag free on domestic itineraries with American Airlines, saving you at least $45 each time. (Note that this is only for domestic flights; I had to pay out of pocket when I traveled to Mexico, forgetting the restrictions of this perk.) Additionally, you'll receive a statement credit of up to $120 for Global Entry/TSA PreCheck. (I suggest maximizing your credit by applying for Global Entry, as it includes PreCheck anyway.) You'll also receive elite status with two partner programs: - Omni Champion, which includes room upgrades, early check-in and late checkout privileges (subject to availability), and an annual free night reward after qualifying stays at participating Omni Hotels properties. - Avis President's Club (through Aug. 31, 2028), providing car rental upgrades (subject to availability), the ability to skip the rental counter at major airports and complimentary additional drivers. Furthermore, the card includes travel protections, such as trip cancellation, trip interruption, trip delay, lost baggage protection and car rental insurance coverage. And there are no foreign transaction fees, making this card a good option for international purchases. Related: Which airline is now best if you don't want to pay bag fees? Elite status If chasing AAdvantage elite status is important to you, the Citi / AA Executive will help you achieve it. You'll earn 1 Loyalty Point for every mile you earn from purchases. Cardholders also earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points after reaching each of the following milestones in the same status qualification year: - 50,000 Loyalty Points - 90,000 Loyalty Points - 165,000 Loyalty Points - 240,000 Loyalty Points Related: 8 methods that earned American AAdvantage Executive Platinum Statement credits The statement credits on the Citi / AA Executive include: - Up to $500 in annual American Airlines Vacations statement credits (up to $250 every six months) - Up to $180 in annual Lyft credits ($15 monthly) — but you have to take three eligible rides each month first to receive this credit - Up to $120 back in statement credits on eligible prepaid rentals booked directly on Avis.com or Budget.com every calendar year - Up to $100 annual statement credit for eligible American Airlines inflight and Admirals Club purchases The American Airlines Vacations credits are only valuable if you'd book these packages anyway. Note that the credit splits into two $250 six-month periods — you must use one in the first half of the year and one in the second; unused credits don't roll over. Qualifying packages typically require at least two travel components (flight plus hotel, flight plus rental car, etc.), though you can often minimize costs by adding a cheap rental car to a flight or hotel booking. I've had issues with the car rental credit, so I wouldn't rely on it for value. Previously, a Budget rental in Cabo was not coded correctly, and Citi wouldn't manually apply the credit. Later, I completed another Budget rental in Ireland and waited the obligatory 10 weeks. Again, it didn't post, and again, Citi refused to apply a manual credit. I don't value the Lyft perk because you don't get the $15 credit until after you've taken three (non-discounted) rides in a month. Instead, I use my Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) to earn 5 points per dollar spent, plus a $10 monthly in-app credit on Lyft purchases (through Sept. 30, 2027). The inflight (and Admirals Club) credit is useful if you regularly buy onboard refreshments or snacks. Related: Frequent Uber or Lyft user? These are the best credit cards for you Earning and redeeming miles If you're looking to supercharge your points earning across several programs, I'd suggest putting your spending on a card that earns transferable points. However, if you want to maximize your AAdvantage mile balance specifically, the Citi / AA Executive will earn you: - 12 miles per dollar spent on eligible car rentals and hotels booked through American's car rental and hotel booking sites, respectively - 4 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases (jumps to 5 miles per dollar spent for the remainder of the calendar year once you've spent $150,000 on purchases in a calendar year) - 1 mile per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases AAdvantage miles are more valuable (at 1.45 cents each) than United MileagePlus miles (1.2 cents) and Delta SkyMiles (1.2 cents), according to our valuations. I redeemed part of the welcome bonus I received on this card for a luxurious flight. I used 70,000 miles plus $174 for a one-way business-class flight in Qatar Airways' fantastic Qsuite from Doha to Houston. Given that this flight retails for $3,910 one-way, I got a very high 5.6 cents per mile from this redemption, quadruple TPG's valuation of AAdvantage miles. Related: The best uses of American Airlines AAdvantage miles Authorized users Finally, the Citi / AA Executive is a great option if you want to extend Admirals Club access to friends and family affordably. You can add up to three authorized users for $175 total (about $58 each), and $175 each after that. Each authorized user receives Admirals Club access (with a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight) for themselves and up to two traveling companions. However, authorized users only get Admirals Club access, not a full Admirals Club membership. Related: Everything you need to know about authorized credit card users Bottom line Ultimately, if you value Admirals Club access, priority perks on American flights and a large welcome bonus, this card can easily justify its fee. You'll get even more value if you take advantage of its statement credits and authorized user perks. But if lounge access isn't important to you, consider one of Citi's lower-fee AAdvantage cards instead. To learn more, read our full review of the Citi / AA Executive World Legend Mastercard. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Ultimate guide to Frontier Miles: How to earn and redeem miles, elite status and more
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.76
Ultimate guide to Frontier Miles: How to earn and redeem miles, elite status and more Editor's Note With its discount fares and robust frequent flyer program, Frontier Miles can offer great value for frequent Frontier Airlines travelers. As a Frontier Miles member, you can earn miles and elite status. Frontier elite status offers multiple perks to make your travels more enjoyable and less expensive, including complimentary luggage, priority boarding and the ability to pool your miles. You can then redeem your miles for award travel. Here's an overview of how the program works. How to earn Frontier points and miles The Frontier Miles program is free to join. It offers two types of rewards: miles redeemable for award flights and elite status points used to reach elite status tiers and get perks like free bags and seat selection. Earn points and miles on eligible Frontier purchases Under its revenue-based mileage accrual system, Frontier Miles allows you to earn based on the dollar amount of your ticket plus any additional products you purchase. For bookings made on or after Sept. 1, how many miles and elite status points you earn depends on your elite status, whether you purchase a basic fare or an Economy, Premium or Business bundle and whether you're a Frontier Airlines World Mastercard® holder. Bundled fares now earn significantly more than basic fares. The information for the Frontier Airlines World Mastercard has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Here are Frontier's current earning rates: | Tier | 2026 qualification | Basic fare | Basic fare, cardmember | Economy, Premium or Business bundle | Economy, Premium or Business bundle, cardmember | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Member (no status) | After enrollment | 1 mile and 1 point per dollar spent | 4 miles and 4 points per dollar spent | 6 miles and 6 points per dollar spent | 12 miles and 12 points per dollar spent | | Elite Silver | 10,000 points | 3 miles and 3 points per dollar spent | 6 miles and 6 points per dollar spent | 8 miles and 8 points per dollar spent | 14 miles and 14 points per dollar spent | | Elite Gold | 20,000 points | 5 miles and 5 points per dollar spent | 8 miles and 8 points per dollar spent | 10 miles and 10 points per dollar spent | 16 miles and 16 points per dollar spent | | Elite Platinum | 50,000 points | 7 miles and 7 points per dollar spent | 10 miles and 10 points per dollar spent | 12 miles and 12 points per dollar spent | 18 miles and 18 points per dollar spent | | Elite Diamond | 75,000 points | 11 miles and 11 points per dollar spent | 14 miles and 14 points per dollar spent | 16 miles and 16 points per dollar spent | 22 miles and 22 points per dollar spent | These rates apply to bookings made on or after Sept. 1. Additionally, select Frontier Airlines World Mastercard holders who use their card for eligible Frontier purchases can earn an additional 5 miles and 1 elite status point per dollar spent. Earn redeemable miles and elite status points with the Frontier Airlines credit card Frontier Airlines partners with Barclays to offer the Frontier Airlines World Mastercard. New cardmembers earn 60,000 bonus miles: 50,000 miles after spending $500 on purchases and paying the annual fee in full in the first 90 days from account opening, plus 10,000 miles after adding an authorized user who makes a purchase in the first 90 days. You can also unlock Elite Gold status for 90 days after making your first purchase in the first 90 days of account opening. You can retain Elite Gold status for 12 months from account opening by spending $3,000 in the first 90 days. The card earns 5 miles per dollar spent on eligible Frontier purchases, 3 miles per dollar spent at restaurants and 1 mile per dollar spent on other purchases. You'll also earn 1 elite status point for every dollar spent on the card. The card offers valuable benefits like Group 4 boarding on all Frontier flights, two free checked bags and family miles pooling. You can also earn a $100 flight voucher each account anniversary after spending $2,500 or more on purchases with your card during the card membership year. Unless you place a high value on Frontier Airlines miles and elite status, we generally don't recommend this card. Most travelers are better off with a transferable points or miles credit card like the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees). Earn miles with Frontier's partners Frontier offers several more ways to earn miles, but keep in mind that these only earn miles, not points toward elite status. Frontier has relationships with several major rental car companies, so you can earn bonus miles and access negotiated rates when booking through Frontier's partner page. While earning rates depend on the rental car company, you can generally earn between 50 and 100 miles per rental, per day or between 500 and 1,000 miles per rental. Frontier Miles also partners with Marriott Bonvoy and Wyndham Rewards. Marriott Bonvoy members can earn 1 to 2 Frontier miles per dollar spent at participating Marriott brands, and Wyndham Rewards members can also earn 1 to 2 Frontier miles per dollar spent at participating hotels, depending on their status. In both cases, you must update your hotel loyalty account preferences to earn Frontier miles instead of hotel points. We don't recommend doing this since you'll typically get a lower return with Frontier miles. For example, basic Bonvoy members earn 10 points per dollar spent at Autograph Collection hotels. According to TPG's September 2026 valuations, which put Bonvoy points at 0.75 cents each, that's a return of 7.5%. Compare that to the 2 Frontier miles per dollar you would earn at Autograph Collection hotels, which provides only a 2.6% return. You also have the option to convert your existing hotel points to Frontier miles. Marriott points transfer to Frontier at a 3:1 ratio, while Wyndham points transfer to Frontier at a 5:1 ratio. Frontier also became a transfer partner of Rove in July 2026. Rove miles transfer to Frontier Miles at a 1:1 ratio, giving members another way to top off a Frontier account without flying or using the Frontier credit card. Frontier has a few other partners to give you more options for earning miles. You can earn 10 miles per dollar spent when you order flowers from Teleflora. Or, you can book a cruise through Frontier Cruises and earn miles at a preset rate: - One- to five-night cruises: 1,500 miles - Six- to eight-night cruises: 3,000 miles - Nine- to 12-night cruises: 5,000 miles - Cruises 13 nights and longer: 10,000 miles This may be a useful option for Frontier loyalists, but you can often earn more miles by booking through other cruise platforms. Lastly, you can buy Frontier miles at 2.5 cents per mile. This is considerably higher than TPG's September 2026 valuation of 1.3 cents per Frontier mile, so we don't advise it in most cases. However, if you're planning a redemption and you're short a few miles, it could make sense. Related: When does it make sense to buy points and miles? How to redeem Frontier miles One-way award flights currently start at the following rates: - Basic: From 5,000 miles - Economy: From 7,000 miles - Premium: From 9,000 miles - Business: From 13,000 miles Frontier says there are no blackout dates for award flights, although the number of miles required varies by flight and availability. Taxes and fees start at $5.60 each way but can increase sharply depending on the destination. | Destination | One-way taxes and fees from | Round-trip taxes and fees from | |---|---|---| | U.S. and Puerto Rico | $5.60 | $11.20 | | Mexico | $40.71 | $126.24 | | Dominican Republic | $46.90 to $49.65 | $115.55 to $121.05 | | Jamaica | $49.60 | $142.42 to $168.70 | | El Salvador | $7.10 | $63.58 | | Bahamas | $6.60 | $116.65 | | Costa Rica | $22.68 to $22.95 | $77.04 to $83.62 | | Guatemala | $5.60 | $55.50 | | Antigua | $43.10 | $97.95 | Redeem miles for add-ons Economy bundles start at just 2,000 miles. If you want to use miles for a bundle, you must select the "Use miles for bundles" option before choosing your flight during the original booking process. Frontier allows bundles to be paired with standard, Discount Den, GoWild and award fares. Considering Frontier provides many add-on options — and has various fees that can quickly stack up, even if you book your ticket with miles — being able to redeem miles for these items could be a great asset for Frontier Miles members. Redeeming your 5,000-mile Super Bowl weekend bonus If you were lucky enough to catch Frontier's Super Bowl weekend promotion (no longer available), you might be wondering how you can use your 5,000 miles. Fortunately, basic award flights now start at 5,000 miles one-way, meaning you can use your entire bonus in one go. For example, you could fly between Denver International Airport (DEN) and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) for just 5,000 miles one-way, plus $6 in taxes and fees. These great deals can be found on longer journeys and even on connecting flights. Flights from San Francisco International Airport (SFO) to Tampa International Airport (TPA) via DEN start from the same 5,000 miles plus $6 in taxes and fees. With this Super Bowl weekend bonus in hand, you'd have enough miles to book either of these redemptions. Frontier's Discount Den membership Frontier Airlines offers a membership program called Discount Den. While not the same as elite status, this program provides access to discounted fares for a $59.99 annual membership fee. New members must also pay a $50 enrollment fee, bringing the first-year cost to $109.99. On "Kids Fly Free" flights, one child under 15 can fly free for every adult Discount Den fare purchased, offering excellent savings on certain routes. We've historically found that Discount Den can offer pretty good deals, too, with savings of $20 per person on both domestic and international tickets. Discount Den can also help you earn Frontier status. The purchase of the Discount Den membership itself earns Frontier miles and elite status points at Frontier's bundle earning rate. We recommend that frequent Frontier flyers consider a Discount Den membership if they expect to save more than $109.99 in their first membership year or more than $59.99 in subsequent years. It's easier to get value from a Discount Den membership when you travel with kids; a family of four may recoup the annual cost with just one family vacation. Frontier's GoWild Pass Frontier Airlines also offers an all-you-can-fly pass called GoWild. Frontier regularly changes the types and prices of GoWild passes it sells. As of September 2026, the carrier is selling its fall and winter pass for $249, which covers travel through Feb. 28, 2027. GoWild flights can be confirmed the day before departure for domestic travel and beginning 10 days before departure for international travel. Frontier sometimes lets members book earlier on select flights for an additional early booking charge. Each flight segment has a fare of 1 cent, but government and airport taxes and fees still apply. You may find unexpectedly high fees and limited availability with this pass, depending on your travel dates and routes. Bags and seat assignments generally cost extra unless your elite status provides them. GoWild can also help you earn elite status. Eligible GoWild ticket purchases earn Frontier miles and elite status points, while the purchase of the GoWild Pass itself earns miles and elite status points at Frontier's bundle earning rates. Related: I bought a Frontier all-you-can-fly pass — here's what it was like to use it Frontier elite status Frontier announced significant changes to its elite status levels in August 2026. Elite Diamond status now requires just 75,000 elite status points, down from 100,000. For the remainder of 2026, Elite Silver status continues to require 10,000 points, Elite Gold status requires 20,000 points and Elite Platinum status requires 50,000 points. Beginning Jan. 1, 2027, the thresholds for Elite Silver and Elite Gold will increase to 15,000 and 25,000 points, respectively, while Elite Platinum and Elite Diamond will require 50,000 and 75,000 points, respectively. When you qualify for Frontier elite status during a calendar year, you can use that status for the remainder of the year in which you qualify and throughout the following calendar year. For example, if you reach an elite status tier in June 2026, you can enjoy that status through Dec. 31, 2027. However, your elite status point balance resets to zero at the beginning of each calendar year for requalification purposes, so you'll need to earn enough points each year to retain or improve your status. The following benefits apply to bookings made through Dec. 31, 2026. Elite Silver status: - No change/cancellation fees (more than seven days before departure) - Priority customer care - Family miles pooling - Standard seat at booking - Preferred seat at check-in - Group 4 boarding (for everyone on booking) Elite Gold status (includes the same benefits as Elite Silver, plus): - Carry-on bag (for only the member) - Preferred seat at booking - Premium seat at check-in - UpFront Plus (four hours before departure) - Group 1 boarding Elite Platinum status (includes the same benefits as Elite Gold, plus): - Carry-on bag (for everyone on booking) - First checked bag (for everyone on booking) - Standard seat at booking (for everyone on booking) - Premium or preferred seat at booking (for the member) - Premium or preferred seat at check-in (for everyone on booking) - UpFront Plus (12 hours before departure) - Group 1 boarding (for everyone on booking) - Companion travel - Pet-in-cabin fee waiver - 50% off Discount Den membership - Ability to gift Elite Silver status Elite Diamond status (includes the same benefits as Elite Platinum, plus): - Refundability (more than one day before departure) - Two checked bags (for everyone on booking) - Premium seat at booking (for everyone on booking) - UpFront Plus (upon check-in, subject to availability) - Priority boarding (for everyone on booking) - Discount Den membership - Ability to gift Elite Gold status Frontier elite status benefits from 2027 Frontier's new elite qualification thresholds take effect Jan. 1, 2027, while the updated elite benefits below apply to bookings made on or after Jan. 1, 2027. Each tier includes the benefits of the tiers below it. Elite Silver, at 15,000 points, will receive complimentary space-available upgrades to UpFront Plus or first class four hours before departure when traveling on an Economy or Premium bundle. Elite Silver members who buy an Economy bundle will also be eligible for upgrades to preferred seating, Group 4 boarding, priority customer care and family pooling. Elite Gold, at 25,000 points, will receive UpFront Plus or first-class upgrades eight hours before departure and premium seat upgrades when purchasing an Economy bundle. Elite Gold also includes a free carry-on bag and Group 1 boarding. Elite Platinum, at 50,000 points, will receive UpFront Plus or first-class upgrades 18 hours before departure and premium seat upgrades for everyone on the reservation when purchasing an Economy bundle. Elite Platinum will also include a free carry-on bag and one checked bag weighing up to 50 pounds for everyone on the booking, plus a waiver of the pet-in-cabin fee. However, the Elite Platinum tier's current unlimited companion travel benefit will be replaced by two companion travel certificates in 2027. Elite Diamond, at 75,000 points, will receive UpFront Plus or first-class upgrades 24 hours before departure, two checked bags weighing up to 50 pounds each for everyone on the reservation, unlimited companion travel and preboarding. Frontier also plans to introduce milestone rewards in 2027. These will let elite members select additional benefits as they progress through the program. The airline has not yet announced the full details. Ways to fast-track Frontier status You don't necessarily have to earn Frontier status solely by buying flights. A few shortcuts can help: - Use the Frontier Airlines World Mastercard: You'll earn 1 elite status point per dollar spent on card purchases, plus enhanced earnings on eligible Frontier bookings. Some card offers may also include a temporary shortcut to Elite Gold status, so check the current application terms. - Buy a Discount Den or GoWild Pass: Frontier treats the purchase price of both memberships as eligible spending that earns miles and elite status points at the applicable bundle rate. - Watch for status matches and promotions: Frontier has offered paid instant-status deals and status matches in the past, so it's worth keeping an eye on its status-match website for new opportunities. Bottom line The Frontier Miles loyalty program can be worthwhile for those who fly the airline often. Award flights start at just 5,000 miles, and members can now redeem miles for bundles starting at 2,000 miles, which can help offset some of the extra costs associated with flying an ultra-low-cost carrier. However, the program became much less rewarding for travelers who book basic fares without a Frontier credit card in September 2026, though its elite status can still be particularly valuable for families and travelers who want to avoid baggage and seat assignment fees. Whether Frontier Miles is worth pursuing ultimately depends on how well Frontier's route network and ultra-low-cost model fit your travel patterns. Status, the cobranded card and memberships like Discount Den can substantially reduce Frontier's add-on costs, but they don't change the carrier's more bare-bones basic fare experience or make sense if you rarely fly Frontier.

item.title: The 10 best places to travel in October 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.44
The 10 best places to travel in October 2026 Editor's Note October is one of the best months to plan a leisure trip. In many popular destinations, it's shoulder season, bringing fewer crowds, lower hotel rates and comfortable weather. In the Northern Hemisphere, it's also prime time for fall foliage, while destinations south of the equator are welcoming spring with blooming flowers and warming temperatures. From leaf-peeping in New England to wine tasting in Vienna and chasing hot air balloons in Japan, these are 10 of the best places to visit in the U.S. and beyond this October. Related: 9 cool hotels for leaf peeping, from Central Park to the Rocky Mountains Zürich, Switzerland In October, Zürich comes to life with fall colors, cultural events and seasonal experiences. A major highlight is the Zurich Film Festival, running from Sept. 24 to Oct. 4. The festival features more than 100 films and a packed lineup of talks, masterclasses and galas featuring filmmakers, actors and other international guests. Just outside the city, Jucker Farm hosts its annual Pumpkin Exhibition through Oct. 25. The family-friendly event features elaborate pumpkin sculptures based on this year's "Bon Voyage" theme, along with a food festival and immersive activities including fruit picking and an apple maze. Later in the month, Expovina Weinschiffe, taking place from Oct. 29 to Nov. 12, transforms the boats at Bürkliplatz into a floating wine fair. The event brings together wine producers and visitors for tastings aboard a fleet of ships overlooking Lake Zürich. Feeling more active? Head to Üetliberg, the mountain overlooking Zürich and just a short train ride from the city center. Its network of trails is especially appealing in autumn, when colorful foliage frames sweeping views of the city, Lake Zürich, and, on clear days, the Alps. TPG tip: Situated in the city's historic Old Town and spanning nine medieval townhouses, the upscale Widder Hotel features 49 unique rooms and suites with thoughtfully preserved details, including ancient frescoes and terracotta flooring. It is also home to the two-Michelin-starred Restaurant Widder, overseen by chef Stefan Heilemann. Nightly rates in October start at $910. Book a stay of two or more nights through American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts to receive daily breakfast for two guests, guaranteed late checkout and a $100 property credit to use on qualifying food and beverages. Asheville, North Carolina While we never need a reason to plan a vacation to Asheville, a visit is also a meaningful way to support the city as it continues to recover after Hurricane Helene. With cool events and festivals happening every day, October is one of the best times of the year to visit. LaZoom's Ghosted! Adult-only Haunted Comedy Tour (Oct. 1 to 31) is a humorous and educational tour aboard the company's signature purple buses. To see Biltmore in a whole new light, check out Luminere at Biltmore (Oct. 1 to 18), an outdoor evening experience that illuminates America's Largest Home and its famous gardens with dynamic visuals and sounds. Other October picks include the family-friendly, corn-themed Eliada Corn Maze and Festival (Oct. 1 to 31); the 369 Monologue and Short Play Festival (Oct. 1 to 18), a celebration of artists of color; and the Craft Fair of the Southern Highlands (Oct. 15 to 18), one of the country's top craft events. Some of the most picturesque spots to take in Asheville's majestic fall foliage include the Blue Ridge Parkway — the views are especially stunning at Black Balsam Knob and Craggy Gardens — as well as Looking Glass Falls and Biltmore Estate. Asheville's dining and drinking scene is unpretentious, but never short on quality. Botiwalla, by James Beard Award-winning chef Meherwan Irani, celebrates India's vibrant street food culture, while Mother turns out hearty sandwiches and sweets, including a cookie bar made with its long-fermented sourdough. For a proper nightcap and dessert, head to Potential New Boyfriend, a colorful, retro-styled lounge serving natural wines and indulgent, ever-rotating ice cream flavors. TPG Tip: Following a sweeping Hurricane Helene restoration, the stately Grand Bohemian Lodge Asheville reopened last year, with updates to its locally curated art program and steakhouse, Red Stag Grill. Rooms are available from $215 or 85,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October. The playful and conveniently located Moxy Asheville Downtown is also a great pick; nightly October rates start at $132 or 47,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. If glamping is your style, book the recently opened AutoCamp Asheville, with charming cabins and airstreams set on 16 scenic acres along the French Broad River. In October, accommodations are available from $256 or 70,000 Hilton Honors points per night. Related: The ultimate Blue Ridge Parkway road trip guide Saga, Japan If you want to visit Japan this fall while avoiding the biggest tourist crowds, consider Saga. This prefecture in northwestern Kyushu is gaining attention for its porcelain, sake and onsen culture — and October brings several can't-miss events. From Oct. 30 to Nov. 3, the Saga International Balloon Fiesta, Asia's largest sky sports event, fills the sky with colorful balloons, including some modeled after animals and cartoon characters. Cycling fans can also plan their trip around the 2026 Tour de Kyushu, an international road race that traverses six prefectures in Kyushu, including Saga on Oct. 10. Mild autumn weather is another draw, with daytime temperatures averaging in the mid-70s. And while Japan is already beloved for its world-class fall foliage, the season also brings a lesser-known but equally spectacular sight: peak cosmos blooms in red, white and pink. One of the best places to see them is Saga's Kinryu Park. TPG Tip: With just 84 rooms, Fairfield by Marriott Saga Ureshino Onsen offers an intimate, comfortable home base for exploring the region's legendary hot springs and rich culinary culture, including green tea and tofu. Rooms start at $78 per night or 17,000 Marriott Bonvoy points in October. Burlington, Vermont With its abundance of native trees (including sugar maples) and mountainous terrain, New England has long been one of the world's most cherished destinations for fall foliage. The catch, naturally, is the crush of crowds. This is where Burlington comes in. Set on the shores of Lake Champlain, Vermont's biggest city balances a small-town feel with urban conveniences — and, of course, spectacular scenery. Plus, the weather this time of year is blissful, averaging in the 50s. For optimal leaf-peeping, visit Centennial Woods, a 65-acre forest on the edge of the University of Vermont campus. For panoramic views of Lake Champlain, take a leisurely hike at Rock Point. Cycling enthusiasts can rent a bike from Local Motion and ride the Island Line Trail, which extends into Lake Champlain and offers spectacular views of the Adirondack Mountains. Burlington's culinary scene is tiny but mighty. The warm and deeply knowledgeable Kate Wise, a 2026 James Beard semifinalist, leads the lively bar at Hotel Vermont's Juniper Bar & Restaurant. Paul Trombly, a 2026 James Beard finalist for Best Chef: Northeast, sends out lovely, mostly plant-based dishes — order the crispy rice and lentil pancakes — at the cozy Fancy's. Fellow 2026 James Beard nominee for Outstanding Restaurateur Leslie Wells recently opened her fourth concept, Alimentari Café & Provisions. To make flying in and out even more comfortable, Leahy Burlington International Airport recently unveiled a $68 million, fossil-fuel-free expansion, complete with a brand-new terminal, more gates and additional amenities — all designed with sustainability in mind. TPG tip: With a prime address in downtown Burlington along Lake Champlain, The Harborvale debuted a few months ago with 161 guest rooms and suites in earthy tones, plus a namesake restaurant specializing in rustic, locally sourced fare. In October, nightly rates start at $274 or 55,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. Vienna If you're an art and culture lover, October is one of the best months to visit Austria's capital. But if you only have a weekend to spare, make it Oct. 3 to 4. This way, you can combine the final days of Vienna Design Week (Sept. 25 to Oct. 4) — one of Europe's top design festivals, celebrating its 20th anniversary this year — with the Long Night of Museums (Oct. 3), when a single ticket gives you access to museums and cultural institutions staying open late for one evening. It's also the opening weekend of the Vienna Drag Festival (Oct. 3 to18). Viennale (Oct. 22 to Nov. 3), Austria's premier international film festival, and Design District (Oct. 9 to 11), an annual showcase of interior design and furniture, are also worth checking out. As October is harvest season in the city's vineyards, set aside some time for wine-related experiences: sipping Wiener Gemischter Satz, Vienna's signature wine, at Heurigen (traditional wine taverns); hiking through the vineyards of Kahlenberg and Nussberg; and hopping aboard the Heurigen Express, a miniature train that loops through the city's wine-growing districts. In case you didn't know, Vienna is an under-the-radar destination for fall foliage. With approximately 1,000 parks and gardens, there are plenty of spots — local picks include the historic Schönbrunn Palace Gardens and the city parks of Stadtpark, Volksgarten and Burggarten — to immerse yourself in the seasonal scenery. TPG Tip: Housed in a beautifully restored 20th-century Art Nouveau building, Mandarin Oriental Vienna blends a posh, residential-style design with all the hallmarks the Hong Kong–based hospitality brand is known for: personalized service, a holistic approach to wellness — including Vienna's largest indoor pool — and elegant dining concepts that attract guests and locals alike. October rates for this American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts member start at $794 per night. Aruba Aruba lives up to its nickname, "One Happy Island," thanks to its consistently sunny weather, location outside the hurricane belt, cooling trade winds and silky beaches. No wonder it's such a popular year-round destination. If your travel dates are flexible, consider arriving during Aruba's low season in October. You'll enjoy lower hotel rates and fewer crowds while experiencing one of the island's biggest events: the Autentico Aruba Culinary Festival. Taking place Oct. 3 to 11, the festival celebrates the culinary traditions of the island's diverse population, reflecting its more than 100 nationalities. Highlights include special prix-fixe menus during Restaurant Week, chef-hosted Bucket List Experiences and the grand finale, The Pavilion. Other October events to mark on your calendar include the inaugural Leyenda del Dorado Aruba (Oct. 9 to 11), a three-day international mountain bike race across the island's craggy terrain, and Interpaso (Oct. 31 to Nov. 1), an international Paso Fino horse competition. Don't forget to pick up some of Aruba Aloe's world-famous skincare — perfect for soothing your sun-kissed skin and equally great for gift-giving — before you head home. TPG Tip: Based on the hotel-within-a-hotel concept, the new The Westerly at Hilton Aruba Caribbean Resort is an oceanfront tower with 161 crisp, airy rooms — the beds are especially dreamy — plus Terrace on 10, an adults-only rooftop retreat available for an additional fee. The indoor-outdoor space pairs stunning waterfront views with well-crafted drinks and all-day dining. Naturally, guests of The Westerly also have access to everything the Hilton resort has to offer, including the eforea Spa, casino and prime stretch of Palm Beach. Rooms are available from $743 or 243,000 Hilton Honors points per night in October. Lancaster County, Pennsylvania If you're after a scenic, culturally rich and delicious fall getaway — just a three-hour Amtrak ride from New York City — consider Lancaster County in south-central Pennsylvania. Home to the oldest and largest Amish community in the United States, the area is known for its bucolic landscape of rolling farmland, quiet streams and historic covered bridges. You'll likely find yourself sharing the road with Amish horse-drawn buggies, too. To learn more about Amish culture, visit the Amish Village, where an authentic 1840 farmhouse, one-room schoolhouse and other historic structures offer a glimpse into traditional Amish life. Opened in May in downtown Lancaster, the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center is a museum and educational center highlighting the lives and legacies of abolitionist and civil rights advocate Thaddeus Stevens and his partner, Lydia Hamilton Smith. Since 1954, Kitchen Kettle Village has grown into a charming destination in its own right, with more than 40 shops, including the iconic Jam & Relish Kitchen, Kling House Restaurant and residential-style accommodations. Lancaster County's restaurant scene offers an enticing mix of old and new. For casual bites, check out Lancaster Central Market, the oldest continuously operated public market in America, and Southern Market, just a few blocks away. Nathan Flaim, a 2026 James Beard Award finalist for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic, has grown Luca into a popular destination for exceptional housemade pastas and small plates that showcase Lancaster's rich bounty. Passerine and Vécu are equally charming brunch options, while Front Porch Baking Co. specializes in loaves and pastries baked with Pennsylvania-grown grains. No trip to Lancaster, however, would be complete without visiting a smorgasbord, a massive buffet including Pennsylvania Dutch comfort foods like potato filling, chicken corn soup and shoofly pie. TPG Tip: Taking up residence in the former Wilbur Chocolate Factory, the 74-key Wilbur Lititz, Tapestry Collection by Hilton retains many of the historic structure's original details — timber beams, exposed brick and arched windows — while incorporating modern touches, from the chocolate scent that infuses the lobby to Kōle Chophouse, a relaxed steakhouse serving Japanese Wagyu fired on a Josper charcoal grill. Nightly October rates start at $216 or 63,000 Hilton Honors points. Seychelles Though Seychelles makes for a great warm-weather vacation any time of year, October holds even more appeal for those seeking sublime weather — hot, sunny and relatively dry, with little wind or rain. The month is also ideal for catching big fish, such as barracuda and various tuna species. The island nation is also renowned for its diverse birdlife, and October provides an opportune time to spot migratory shorebirds like Pacific golden plovers and breeding seabirds, including sooty terns. The Creole Festival, an annual celebration of the archipelago's unique tapestry of African, European and Asian influences, will be hosted in the country's lively capital of Victoria during the last week of October. TPG tip: The all-villa Cheval Blanc Seychelles marks the sixth property in LVMH's swanky Cheval Blanc portfolio, and the first in Africa. Receive daily breakfast for two, late checkout and more when you book via the Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts program. Nightly rates in October start at $2,600. Puebla, Mexico Puebla is the antidote for those weary of touristy Mexico City and Tulum. Despite being Mexico's fourth-biggest city, Puebla balances everything you want from a well-rounded vacation destination — restaurants, shopping, history — with a neighborly, small-town feel. October is one of the best times to visit, as the month marks the transition from the rainy season to the dry season, with average daytime highs in the mid- to high 70s. Even better? It's easy to experience the best of Puebla in one weekend. Meander through the city's UNESCO-listed historic center, filled with colorful 16th- and 17th-century churches and other religious structures. As Puebla is the birthplace of mole poblano, the famously complex sweet-savory sauce, try as many versions as possible while you're in town. Some of the best can be found at the Michelin Guide-recommended Augurio, from beloved local chef Ángel Vázquez, as well as Comal and Mural de los Poblanos. It's also worth shopping for talavera, the region's colorful, hand-painted ceramics. TPG tip: A member of American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts, Banyan Tree Puebla is a 78-room property that celebrates Pueblan culture from its design to its offerings, including the highly recommended mole cooking class. Rooms in October start at $195 per night. Brisbane, Australia No longer hiding in the shadows of Sydney and Melbourne, Brisbane — Australia's third-largest city and Queensland's capital — has blossomed into a worldly yet laid-back destination. With pleasant October temperatures hovering in the mid- to high 70s, Brisbane is an urban paradise for outdoor lovers, whether you want to soak in the rays at Streets Beach (a unique human-made beach) or get up close to wildlife at Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary. The city's restaurant landscape has also been attracting attention, with the ambitious tasting-menu concept Exhibition, wood-fired Agnes and intimate August, housed in a refurbished 137-year-old heritage church, leading the charge. TPG tip: Since 2018, the W Brisbane has been one of the city's hippest places to hang your hat. Rooms are available from $360 or 48,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October.

item.title: Spacious suites and fine wines: A review of United's new Elevated Polaris business class
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.15
Spacious suites and fine wines: A review of United's new Elevated Polaris business class Quick take: United's new "Elevated" Polaris business class represents a sophisticated step forward for the airline. Hopefully the closing privacy doors will be certified soon. Pros - There's decent award availability for United cardholders. - Seats are spacious and have closing doors. - Upscale food and beverage service with pre-order is available. Cons - Privacy doors need to be certified before they can be used. - Wi-Fi isn't free and is slower than Starlink. - The sound systems in the seats seem to have a few bugs. TPG got the first peek at United's swanky new "Elevated" Polaris business class in March when the airline showed off the fancy new suite-style pods at an event in Los Angeles shortly after flights went on sale. Senior aviation reporter Sean Cudahy was also among the first to actually fly in the new suites when he boarded the inaugural flight from San Francisco to Singapore in April. Sean actually flew in the enhanced "Studio" version of the suites, which are in the bulkhead row and cost a premium. So I took it upon myself to be TPG's guinea pig and fly the standard version of the seat on my own way from Singapore to San Francisco a couple of weeks ago. The new Elevated Polaris feels like a timely step forward for the airline, with amenities and other soft touches that loyal United flyers have come to expect. Here's what it was like flying nearly 16 hours in United's new business class and how to book it for yourself. How much does it cost to book United's Elevated Polaris business class? The cost of a long-haul, business-class ticket in United's new Elevated Polaris business class depends on the route, dates and whether you are flying round-trip or one-way. My one-way flight from Singapore Changi International Airport (SIN) to San Francisco International Airport (SFO) cost me 90,000 United MileagePlus miles plus $74.23 in taxes and fees instead of a paid fare of $4,148. That yielded me a value of about 4.5 cents per mile, soundly beating TPG's September 2026 valuation of United miles. It was free to choose a regular Polaris seat, but upgrading to a Studio seat would have cost $599 in advance. However, the price dropped to $499 when I checked in. Other passengers must have taken that offer since the five empty Studios I could see on the seat map had filled in by the time we departed. My 90,000-mile award ticket was the lowest level I could find for this route for the entire next year. What's more, it was only available to me because I am a United cobranded credit card holder. Without a United credit card or United Premier status, I would have needed a whopping 250,000 miles. The best way to increase your number of United miles quickly — and to unlock that preferential redemption rate — is to apply for one of the following cobranded credit cards: - United Gateway℠ Card (see rates and fees): 2 bonus miles per dollar spent on United purchases - United℠ Business Card (see rates and fees): 2 bonus miles per dollar spent on United purchases - United Club℠ Business Card: 2 bonus miles per dollar spent on United purchases - United℠ Explorer Card (see rates and fees): 3 bonus miles per dollar spent on United purchases - United Quest℠ Card (see rates and fees): 4 bonus miles per dollar spent on United purchases - United Club℠ Card (see rates and fees): 5 bonus miles per dollar spent on United purchases The information for the United Club Business has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. The good news is, there seems to be plenty of availability on this route, especially in the direction I flew, for that same 90,000 miles — even if you tag on another leg to your final destination within the U.S. Checking into and boarding United business class United Polaris business-class passengers can enjoy the following services at the airport. | Priority check-in | Yes | |---|---| | Luggage allowance | Two checked bags up to 70 pounds (32 kgs) each | | Lounge access | Yes | | Does the airline participate in TSA PreCheck? | Yes | | Priority boarding | Yes | My flight departed from Singapore Changi's Terminal 2. There were dedicated check-in lines for economy and Premier Access, which I could access thanks to my business-class ticket. I checked my bag, cleared immigration in a matter of minutes, and then made my way to Singapore Airlines' business-class KrisFlyer Lounge. I only spent a few minutes there getting a coffee since it was rush hour and nearly every seat was taken, but you can expect a variety of seating areas and an extensive buffet with live cooking stations for items like egg dishes and soup. Just over an hour before departure time, I made the 15-minute walk to the gate, which was just opening up for security checks. Boarding began right on time, 55 minutes before departure, and I was the first on board. How comfortable is United's Elevated Polaris business class? You can currently find United's Elevated Polaris cabins aboard a handful of newly delivered Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners. Each plane features an enormous premium section spanning the front half of the aircraft, with a total of 64 Polaris seats, including eight premium Studios. The business-class section of the plane is split into two large cabins, each with eight rows of four seats. Here's a quick look at the layout. | Number of seats | 64 (8 Studios and 56 regular seats) | |---|---| | Cabin layout | 1-2-1 | | Seat recline | 78 inches fully flat | | Seat width | 21 inches | | Screen size | 19 inches | All the seats along the sides of the plane are angled out toward the window, so you're not really looking at other passengers. What's interesting is that in the forward cabin, the center seats are angled toward one another with their seatbacks farther apart, while in the back cabin, the center seats have their seatbacks closer to one another and their footrests toward the aisle. For that reason, those back seats might be better for companions traveling together. All the center seats have huge privacy partitions that can be raised, though. | Best seats for solo travelers | Best seats for couples | |---|---| | A and L seats along the sides | Rows 9-17 F and D seats | The biggest evolution of this new Elevated Polaris product is the fact that the seats have substantial sliding doors for privacy, so you can cocoon yourself away from the activity on the aisle. Unfortunately, the plane I was on had only been delivered recently, and the doors had not yet been certified, according to the crew, so they were locked in the open position. I guess I'll just need to test them out on another flight! Jokes aside, I found the footprint to be roomy and provide plenty of privacy. The new Polaris seats also look more sophisticated than their predecessors, thanks to a moody palette of textured graphite-gray exterior shells with navy-blue interior walls, silvery-gray seating upholstery with accent cross-stitching, faux-marble shelving and caramel-colored woodgrain paneling. The aesthetic feels more sultry and elegant than the old Polaris' cheerier sky-blue and brushed-chrome combination. The Studios comprise the four seats in the two bulkhead rows and have a roomier footprint, larger entertainment screens than the regular seats, an ottoman that can double as a companion's dining perch and some extra amenities and food and beverage options on board. The regular seats have a few stowage options, including a small compartment next to the seatback with a mirror where you can tuck in provided noise-canceling headsets and amenity kits. There is another small compartment with a water bottle holder in the aisle-side armrest that can be raised or lowered up to 11 inches. As I mentioned, these seats have doors that will eventually close, and I measured them at 54 inches from the top to the floor. The gap between the armrest and the preceding seat shell is 9 inches. So, it can be a tight squeeze, but it's pretty standard. The ledge next to the seat on this side has a glossy faux-marble shelf and a wireless charging pad for phones that juiced my iPhone 17 Pro by about 1% every five minutes. Next to that is a corded remote for the entertainment system. Beneath this shelf and labeled with helpful icons, there is a universal power plug and two USB-C ports (so if you have older devices, you might need to bring a USB-C to A converter). Now for the fun part: In addition to buttons for preset seating positions, you could control the individual components of the seat using a touchscreen pad near the armrest. It took me a while to get the hang of it since it's sort of like a scrolling scale, but it was fun to use. This pad could also control the lights and even change the color palette to suit your mood. I spent way too much time playing with that feature. The seat's 19-inch OLED 4K entertainment system is also a touchscreen, and the massive tray table deploys from below that. It can be unfolded to a whopping 24-by-16-inch surface with plenty of space for a meal service tray and my MacBook Air at the same time. When it came time to rest, I reclined the seat to its full 78-inch lie-flat length, which was plenty long for me but might not be quite enough for taller travelers. The foot cubby is 12 inches tall and 16 inches wide at its opening, so that was enough space for me to roll over from one side to the other without knocking my toes; however, if you have really large feet, you might feel constrained. Business-class passengers share four lavatories (one per 16 passengers). Two are behind the flight deck near the front galley, and the other two are by the second galley. Given the length of this flight, they only really got busy just after meal service, and the crew did their best to keep them clean. There was a mix of Perricone MD and Therabody products included. Finally, I appreciated the overhead air nozzles, as they kept my seat cool when the cabin was otherwise a little too warm for me. Most passengers were also considerate and kept their windows' electronic shades set to the darkest mode for most of the flight so that everyone could rest. Amenities in United's Elevated Polaris business class These may be new seats, but passengers will still find the airline's signature (and beloved) Saks Fifth Avenue bedding on board. Each seat came stocked with a bedding set that included a firm cooling gel pillow for lumbar support, a soft medium-size pillow, a lightweight blanket that I used as a seat pad and a more substantial duvet wrapped in plastic. The only thing I would have preferred is for the larger pillow to also have a wrap so I could stow it until I needed it. I just kept it down in the seat rather than try to stick it in the overhead, though, so I could keep it clean. I also found a pair of soft slippers on the seat's ottoman and donned them for most of the flight rather than wearing my own shoes. There was a colorful blue-striped Brooks Brothers amenity kit stocked with the following products, including skincare items from Perricone MD: - A toothbrush and toothpaste - Ear plugs - Eye mask - Socks - Tissues - Pen - Perricone MD Vitamin C cleansing wipe - Perricone MD Vitamin C eye gel - Perricone MD Vitamin C hand cream - Perricone MD Vitamin C face mist - Perricone MD Vitamin C lip balm The inclusions were nice, and I actually appreciated how compact the kit itself was, making it easy to stow in the seat-side compartment. The entertainment system felt very advanced. It was a 19-inch HD screen with accessibility options, and it was very easy to navigate. Luckily, it also had Bluetooth capability, so I could connect my own earbuds when the seat's headphone jack was not working properly. (Apparently, this has been a widely reported issue.) Once I did connect, though, the sound was good, and I appreciated the selection of movies and TV shows. Among the new releases were "The Devil Wears Prada 2," "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie" and "Project Hail Mary." The television shows included selections from HBO, including "House of the Dragon" and "Rooster." United is currently rolling out Starlink Wi-Fi, which is free to MileagePlus members on equipped planes. Unfortunately, this Dreamliner wasn't one of them. MileagePlus members could select a free messaging plan for phones that worked well enough on my iPhone for texting and WhatsApp, but not for email or any other apps. Instead, I sprung for the full-flight paid Wi-Fi plan, which was available for a mere $8. It was sufficient for email and some light browsing, and it was easy to swap service between my laptop and phone. How was the food in United's Elevated Polaris business class? After most of the business-class cabin boarded, flight attendants came by offering a choice of water or Gambino prosecco, which retails for about $10. I stuck to water since United has recently upgraded its inflight wines, and I was waiting for the good stuff. The airline allows you to preorder your meals in business class up to 24 hours in advance, and there was one main course choice of salmon available exclusively for preorder. I ordered one of the other dishes in advance to be sure they would have it. Service began about 20 minutes into the flight with a choice of beverages and a little ramekin of warmed nuts. About 20 minutes and another beverage service after that, the staff brought out the first course, which included a choice of: - Spiced seared prawns with chorizo dukkah and cauliflower puree - Mozzarella with charred grapes and balsamic vinegar cream - Baby greens salad with cherry tomatoes, Parmesan and marinated artichoke hearts They served entrees about an hour into the flight. Options included: - Beef tenderloin with rosemary Parmesan Hasselback potatoes, ratatouille and demi-glace - Frenched bone-in chicken breast with creamy polenta, broccolini and caramelized onion demi-glace - Orechiette pasta with white fava bean puree, sundried tomatoes and sauteed mixed vegetables - Seared salmon with braised lentils, asparagus and lemon-thyme butter (the preorder option) I had the beef, and while the piece of meat was well-cooked, the potato that came with it was more like a plain baked potato; the ratatouille was mainly chopped bell peppers in the semi-sweet demi-glace sauce, so I mostly scraped that off. For dessert, there was a choice of: - Made-to-order ice cream sundaes - Lemon pound cake - Cheese plate with fresh fruit I couldn't resist the sundae with the works, and the flight attendant assigned to my row made it expertly. Among the wines on offer were: - Laurent-Perrier La Cuvee Brut Champagne - Stony Hill SHV chardonnay from Napa Valley, California - Chateau Guiraud G Bordeaux Blanc from France - Whispering Angel Rosé from France - Shafer One Point Five cabernet sauvignon from Napa Valley - Lingua Franca Avni pinot noir from Oregon - Taylor Fladgate Late Bottled Vintage Port There was also a variety of sodas, juices, Illy coffee, Twinings teas and beers like Michelob Ultra, Stella Artois and Bell's Two Hearted IPA. As you can see, United has really stepped up its wine game with that Champagne and the cabernet sauvignon, in particular, which retails for well over $100 a bottle. It tasted great in the air, too. Between meals, there were oranges, bananas and potato chips in the galley, and you could also request instant noodle soup. However, the most interesting meal choice was actually the light option, which you could order up to two hours before arrival. It was dubbed a "Tapas" selection and included up to four of the following dishes to mix and match: - Hainan chicken and rice with bok choy and carrots, inspired by Singapore's Maxwell Hawker Centre - Vegetarian curry puff - Laksa with noodles, prawns, fish cake, hard-boiled egg and sambal - Soba noodles with goma dressing, chili oil, edamame and enoki mushrooms I ordered one of each, and the flight attendant came back with the tray around three minutes later. Honestly, I should have just had this as my main meal since the dishes were light, fresh and flavorful, providing a little taste of Singapore. After that meal, I snoozed a little longer and then worked for a few hours. About 90 minutes before arrival, the crew turned on the cabin lights and began serving a prearrival meal. The choice of main dishes included: - Poached shrimp with chicken broth congee, ginger and scallions - Chive scrambled eggs with chicken sausage, potato rosti and roasted tomatoes - Ricotta pancakes with caramelized banana, honeycomb butter and toasted walnuts I had the poached shrimp in congee, and the ginger and scallions lent the dish some much-needed flavor. The tray also came with a bowl of fresh fruit and a croissant. All the meal services were efficient and well-executed. I would rethink my main meal order, and perhaps just go for the tapas course since it was much tastier and more interesting than the two regular meal services. If it's available on your flight, I recommend trying that. One piece of advice: If you're interested in what's on the food and beverage menu for your flight, you can check your flight's status on the United website, click on the button for "inflight menu" and select your class of service to see the options listed. Would you recommend United's Elevated Polaris business class? United's new Elevated Polaris business class is an exciting new option for flyers on the airline's long-haul routes. Hopefully, award availability will continue to be good as more freshly delivered Dreamliners with the new seats on board come online. I also hope to fly the seats again to try out the roomier Studios and to test out whether closing doors improve the experience. For now, though, the new Polaris product is a great way to fly from San Francisco to both Singapore and London, and I'll be on the lookout for more opportunities to try it out. Related reading:

item.title: Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.60
Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel Editor's Note The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card is a great choice for beginners and experienced points-and-miles enthusiasts who want an easy way to earn miles with minimal effort — all for an affordable $95 annual fee. The Venture Rewards card's current welcome offer is especially compelling: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Here's what the offer is worth and what to know before applying. Capital One Venture Rewards welcome offer New Capital One Venture Rewards cardholders can earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Including the credit, this offer is worth $1,688, per TPG's September 2026 valuations. In terms of miles alone, this is the standard welcome bonus on the card. However, the inclusion of the $300 credit makes this offer among the most valuable we've seen. For comparison, previous welcome offers have gone as high as 100,000 miles after meeting the minimum spending requirements (no longer available), but with no credit. It's possible to squeeze even more from that bonus if you redeem Capital One miles for maximum value, thanks to their impressive roster of 15-plus transfer partners. Who is eligible for the Venture Rewards welcome bonus? There are some eligibility requirements to keep in mind before applying. You don't want to waste a hard pull on your credit report if you aren't eligible for the current offer. First, if you've previously earned a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards, you won't be able to earn another one for 48 months. Note that this is 48 months from the date you received your bonus, not from the date you were approved. In addition, if you previously earned a welcome bonus on the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card, you will more than likely not be eligible to earn a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards. Capital One may consider multiple factors when deciding whether to approve you; for a deeper dive into its application requirements, check out our full guide. Related: The best Capital One credit cards Earning Capital One miles This card earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on all purchases. So, by spending $4,000 on it to earn the welcome bonus, you'd earn at least 83,000 miles in the first few months, including the welcome bonus. And since the Venture Rewards earns 5 miles per dollar spent on car rentals, hotels and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel, it's possible to earn even more miles while working toward your welcome bonus. While some travel credit cards may earn slightly higher rates on select categories such as groceries or dining, the draw here is the simplicity and guarantee of earning at least 2 miles per dollar spent on anything you buy without the need to memorize multiple bonus spending categories. Related: Why I keep the Capital One Venture Rewards card in my wallet What can Capital One Miles get you? Your total value from this welcome bonus depends largely on how you redeem your miles. There are two key options: - Redeem for 1 cent apiece toward travel - Redeem by transferring to Capital One's 15-plus partner airlines and hotels (our recommendation) When converting your miles to hotel points or airline miles, most partners offer a 1:1 transfer ratio, though a couple of partners have different ratios. You can get great sweet spot redemptions by transferring miles to programs like Air Canada Aeroplan and Air France-KLM Flying Blue. For example, TPG's editor-in-chief, Nick Ewen, transferred 117,000 Capital One miles to Emirates Skywards to upgrade himself and two family members to Emirates first class. This broke down to 39,000 miles per person, a reasonable cost for the upgrade. If you don't want to transfer your miles, you can redeem them by booking a trip through Capital One Travel. These redemptions can be very handy in a world where you may be renting recreational vehicles, booking vacation home rentals or securing a cabin close to home more often than hopping on a flight to the other side of the world. Related: Cashing in Capital One miles? How to get the maximum value when redeeming miles Other Venture Rewards perks The Capital One Venture Rewards doesn't offer the same benefits as more premium travel rewards cards, including its upscale sibling, the Capital One Venture X Rewards. But for its modest $95 annual fee, the Venture Rewards provides some useful benefits: - An up to $120 statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees - Car rental insurance - Complimentary concierge service - Extended warranty protection - No foreign transaction fees Related: Chase Sapphire Preferred Card vs. Capital One Venture Rewards Bottom line The Capital One Venture Rewards remains a strong option for travelers who value simplicity. It earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on purchases and gives cardholders access to Capital One's airline and hotel transfer partners, all for a $95 annual fee. Plus, the current welcome offer includes a solid haul of miles and a $300 credit for Capital One Travel, one of the best offers we've seen. Just remember to use your credit in the first cardholder year, or you'll forfeit the value. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Venture Rewards card. Learn more: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: A New York City foodie's secret to saving on restaurants? Blackbird's dining loyalty program
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.54
A New York City foodie's secret to saving on restaurants? Blackbird's dining loyalty program New York City has some of the best independent restaurants and coffee shops in the world. It's one of the reasons why I love living here, but it also means dining is easily my largest expense outside of rent each month — and most dining loyalty programs that help you save money at the places you eat at regularly are centered around national chains. Enter Blackbird. Blackbird is a loyalty program and payment app designed for independent restaurants and cafes. A friend introduced me to it earlier this year, and I've since fallen in love with it. You can earn and redeem rewards, access special perks, split and pay your bill and more via the app. The program even has elite status tiers that offer more value. For anyone unfamiliar, I'm breaking down all the program's pros and cons to help you decide if it's worth investing your time and energy. Why Blackbird is a game changer for big-city dining Blackbird allows you to earn Fly rewards points at member restaurants when you check in via the app. The more you check in and spend, the more valuable each visit becomes thanks to the program's loyalty tiers. Those just joining will earn 3 Fly points per dollar spent, but you can earn up to 7 Fly points per dollar spent at the highest Blackbird Club loyalty tier. Right now, Blackbird is available in nine destinations: - New York City (including all boroughs, plus Jersey City and Hoboken, New Jersey) - The Hamptons, New York - Charleston, South Carolina - Los Angeles - San Francisco - Denver - Aspen, Colorado - Vail, Colorado - Breckenridge, Colorado The list of participating restaurants is still growing, but there's a solid number of available spots in New York City currently — from easy weeknight dinner spots like Barn Joo to chains like Tacombi to cocktail bars like The Tusk Bar. I also took a look at available options in Blackbird's other locations. Understandably, New York City has the largest concentration of participating restaurants, but the other major cities on the list have a decent selection of restaurants, too. Checking in is as easy as tapping your phone to the small black Blackbird puck at the host stand, and it's easy to pay your bill (or split it among friends) directly in the app. The best part? You can even stack rewards with your credit card to double up on earning. For example, if you use your American Express® Gold Card to pay your bill through Blackbird, you'll earn Fly points and 4 American Express Membership Rewards points per dollar spent (on up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar). Related: Best credit cards for dining Blackbird Club tiers If you spend enough with Blackbird throughout the year, you'll get access to higher earning rates and additional benefits via the tiered loyalty program. You get access to higher tiers of the program by spending with Blackbird Pay or preloading money into your Blackbird account to use at checkout (similar to how you can preload money into your Starbucks Rewards account).
