Here's a quick breakdown of each tier: | Elite status tier | How to qualify | Earning rates | Key benefits | |---|---|---|---| | Member | Spend $500 in a calendar year, or preload $250 to your Blackbird account. | | N/A | | Regular | Spend $5,000 in a calendar year, or preload $2,500 to your Blackbird account. | | | | Friends & Family | Spend $10,000 in a calendar year, or preload $5,000 to your Blackbird account. | | | I wouldn't recommend preloading money into Blackbird to hit any of the elite tiers, as that would limit your ability to double-dip with credit card rewards when paying the bill at the restaurant, but if you do spend enough at Blackbird restaurants throughout the year to gain access to elevated earning rates, priority reservations and concierge help, those are all potentially valuable benefits. The value breakdown Earning and redeeming with Blackbird is surprisingly straightforward. Depending on your status level, you'll earn between 3 and 7 Fly points per dollar spent, and 100 Fly points equals $1 in spending power toward future Blackbird purchases. That means that even at the free level, you're getting a 3% return on spending, which is on par with a lot of credit card earning rates (and remember, you can also earn credit card points or miles on top of your Blackbird earnings). At the highest member tier, you'll get an impressive 7% return on spending. Blackbird also offers opt-in challenges that let you earn additional Fly points (including a first-time user challenge) and a referral bonus, making it really easy to get immediate value from the program even after just one purchase. A concrete example: I spent $45.30 at a Mexican-focused Tacombi location for my first-ever check-in and got 4,095 points total (3 points per dollar spent on the bill, plus a referral bonus and a first-time bonus). Given that points are worth 1 cent each, I had nearly $41 to spend on a future Blackbird Pay bill. The downsides of Blackbird I have laid out many of the pros in this article already, but there are also some downsides to consider. Only nine destinations are currently participating, and within each, only select restaurants are available. In New York City and the other major participating metropolitan areas, like San Francisco and Los Angeles, you'll have plenty of options where you can earn rewards, but even in the Big Apple, the reality is that the majority of restaurants in the city aren't currently on Blackbird. In the Colorado mountain towns where Blackbird operates (Vail, Breckenridge and Aspen), your options for Blackbird are fairly limited. Another con is that the bill split feature doesn't allow you to itemize. If your friend group tends to share food or split things evenly regardless of itemization, that's not an issue. But if you want to itemize, you'll have to do it the old-fashion way: Pick one person to get the full tab, calculate each person's share separately and then settle via Venmo or Cash App. Who will find Blackbird most valuable? Blackbird has the potential to be a really valuable program — but only for the right user. Consider joining if you're: - A foodie who lives where Blackbird operates. Until Blackbird adds more cities, this program is only valuable to those who eat out often in the nine destinations where Blackbird is currently available. - Someone who often eats family-style meals and splits the bill with friends. The ability to split the bill directly in the app is a great benefit for friend groups like mine, where everyone wants to earn credit card points and miles on the meal. We tend to split things evenly instead of itemizing, so it works perfectly for us. - Regularly spending at least $500 on dining a year. Spending $500 per year will get you Member status and an elevated 4 points per dollar spent earning rate. If you also happen to have the Amex Gold, which offers 4 points per dollar spent on dining worldwide (on up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar), you'll earn a total of 8 points per dollar spent on every qualifying meal. - An adventurous eater who likes trying a variety of restaurants. With Blackbird, you don't have to commit to being loyal to a single restaurant or chain to earn or redeem rewards. Bottom line I love a good travel redemption as much as the next girl, but there's something to be said about an easy way to earn rewards and benefits on an everyday expense like dining. Blackbird is straightforward to use, earns valuable rewards at an array of restaurants and allows me to stack rewards with my credit cards of choice. That's a no-brainer for someone like me who lives in an expensive city like New York and dines out at least once a week with friends. Know, though, that we've seen this movie before with loyalty programs that offer huge sign-up incentives and high earnings without fees. In some ways, this program feels a little too good to be true to me, and, usually, that means it is too good to be true in the long term. (Looking at you, MoviePass.) Still, the current earnings are simply too impressive to ignore, so I'm going to make the most of this program while its points are valuable and its earning rates are high, no matter which status I hold. If you sign up for the program, I'd recommend you do the same. TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Which simple business cash-back card wins?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.50
Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Which simple business cash-back card wins? As a business owner myself, I've spent more brain power than I'd like to admit thinking about which credit cards can help me get more out of my business spending. Two cards that often come up when you're looking for a simple, no-annual-fee business card are the Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card (see rates and fees) and Capital One Spark Cash Select — and it's easy to see why they're competitors. Both keep earning simple, offer tools and benefits for business owners and don't charge an annual fee. At the end of the day, though, the Ink Business Unlimited has an edge for most business owners, especially if you can pair it with an eligible Chase Ultimate Rewards card. I've already put more thought into business credit cards than any reasonable person should, so let me break it down for you. Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: At a glance | | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Annual fee | $0 | $0 | | Welcome bonus | Earn $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months after account opening. | Earn a one-time $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. | | Employee card fee | $0 | $0 | | Base earning rate | Unlimited 1.5% cash back | Unlimited 1.5% cash back | Quick picks by business type | Best for ... | Card | |---|---| | Business owners who already earn Chase Ultimate Rewards points | Ink Business Unlimited | | Those who want more time to finance a large purchase | Ink Business Unlimited | | Those who already earn Capital One miles | Capital One Spark Cash Select | | Those who make purchases abroad | Capital One Spark Cash Select | Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Welcome bonus The Ink Business Unlimited currently offers $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months after account opening. The Spark Cash Select offers a one-time $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. The Ink's bonus is $250 higher, but you'll need to spend an additional $2,000 to earn it. If that level of spending is already normal for your business, the extra $250 is an easy win. But don't spend more than you otherwise would just to chase a bigger bonus. Eligibility is important to consider, too. Chase's application terms say the Ink Business Unlimited bonus may not be available if you've ever had this card or another no-annual-fee Chase business card. Meanwhile, Capital One states that the bonus may not be available to existing or previous Capital One Business cardholders. Winner: Ink Business Unlimited. Assuming you can comfortably meet the higher spending requirement, the extra $250 makes it the better offer. Related: The ultimate guide to credit card application restrictions Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Benefits Neither card is going to wow you with a long list of amazing perks — but that's hardly a surprise for a business card with no annual fee. However, both options offer more protection than you might expect, including extended warranty coverage and rental car insurance. | Benefit | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Employee cards | No additional cost | No additional cost | | Auto rental coverage | Primary for business rentals; up to $60,000 for most eligible vehicles | Primary for eligible business and international rentals* | | Purchase protection | Up to $10,000 per item for 120 days; $50,000 annual account limit | Up to $10,000 per item for 90 days; $50,000 annual account limit* | | Extended warranty protection | Adds one year to eligible warranties of three years or less | Doubles eligible warranties of 12 months or less, up to one additional year* | | Roadside assistance | Yes; cardholder pays for services | Yes; cardholder pays for services | | Foreign transaction fee | 3% | None | *Capital One Mastercard benefits are subject to issuer participation. Check your card's Guide to Benefits for applicable coverage. There's quite a bit of overlap between the two cards. Both offer extended warranty protection, purchase protection and rental car coverage, although the exact terms and coverage limits differ. The Ink Business Unlimited has an edge on purchase protection. Eligible purchases are covered against damage or theft for 120 days (up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per account per year), whereas the Spark Cash Select only covers up to 90 days (with the same limits). The rental car comparison is closer than it first appears. Ink provides primary coverage when renting for business purposes, with reimbursement of up to $60,000 for theft and collision damage for most eligible vehicles. Depending on your card's applicable Mastercard benefits, Spark's MasterRental coverage can also be primary for eligible business rentals and rentals outside your home country. With primary coverage, you shouldn't have to file a claim with your personal auto insurer first. Spark, meanwhile, has an advantage if your business takes you abroad. It charges no foreign transaction fees, compared with 3% on the Ink Business Unlimited. Winner: Tie. Ink offers longer purchase protection and straightforward primary rental car coverage for eligible business rentals, while Spark counters with competitive protections and no foreign transaction fees. Related: Why nearly every purchase should be on a credit card How to earn and redeem rewards with the Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select At first glance, there's not much separating these cards when it comes to earning rewards. Both earn at least 1.5% back on everyday purchases, with no spending caps to track. | Purchase | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Everyday purchases | 1.5% cash back | 1.5% cash back | | Lyft rides | 5% cash back through (Sept. 30, 2027) | 1.5% cash back | | Hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel | 1.5% cash back | 5% cash back | The Spark Cash Select has the edge on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel, earning 5% cash back. The Ink Business Unlimited has a 5% category for Lyft rides through (Sept. 30, 2027), but it's a temporary perk with a much narrower use case. Winner on earning: Spark Cash Select. Both cards earn the same 1.5% on everyday purchases, but Spark's 5% return on Capital One Business Travel bookings gives it a leg up. Redeeming rewards Cash back is the easiest way to use rewards with either card. But if you're willing to do a little more work, both cards have the potential to become much more useful for travel. You can convert the cash back you earn on the Ink Business Unlimited to points with an eligible Ultimate Rewards card, such as the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (see rates and fees) or Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees). Doing so lets you transfer those points to Chase's airline and hotel partners. The Spark Cash Select works similarly. If you have an eligible Capital One miles-earning card, you can convert your cash back into Capital One miles and transfer those miles to Capital One's airline and hotel partners. Neither program is automatically better for travel, either. Chase and Capital One have different airline and hotel transfer partners, so the better option depends largely on which programs you actually use. If you already earn rewards with Chase or Capital One, that's an even stronger reason to stick with the same program and combine your rewards rather than starting from scratch with the other. Winner on redeeming: Tie. Both cards make cash back easy, while pairing either with an eligible card can open the door to transferable travel rewards. Related: How (and why) you should earn transferable credit card points Can I have both the Ink Business Unlimited and Spark Cash Select? Yes. Since one card is issued by Chase and the other by Capital One, there's nothing stopping you from holding both. But you'll still need to qualify for each card individually. For the Ink Business Unlimited, keep Chase's 5/24 rule in mind. You'll need to be under 5/24 to qualify, though most business cards won't count toward your 5/24 total. Capital One doesn't have a publicly stated rule comparable to Chase's 5/24 rule, but you'll still need to meet the issuer's current application requirements to qualify for the Spark Cash Select. But do you actually need both? Probably not. Since both earn at least 1.5% cash back on all purchases, there's a lot of overlap. And with several cash-back cards earning 2% on everyday spending, neither is the strongest choice based on its base earning rate alone. These cards are a better fit if you value simplicity, want to avoid an annual fee or already earn rewards with Chase or Capital One. But if you're starting from scratch, I'd look at options like the Wells Fargo Signify Business Cash® Card (see rates and fees), which earns 2% cash rewards on purchases, or the The American Express Blue Business Cash® Card, which earns 2% cash back on all eligible purchases (up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1% back on all purchases). Related: The best business credit cards to add to your wallet Should I get the Ink Business Unlimited or Spark Cash Select? Choose the Ink Business Unlimited if you already have or want to get a Chase Ultimate Rewards-points earning credit card. Choose the Spark Cash Select if you regularly make international purchases or book hotels and rental cars through Capital One Business Travel. It's also a natural fit if you already have a Capital One travel card and can combine your rewards for more redemption options. Related: Your guide to the Chase Ink Business credit cards Bottom line After weighing it all, Chase's Ink Business Unlimited comes out ahead, but just barely. Its useful protections and the potential to get more from your rewards by pairing it with another Ultimate Rewards card give it the edge. Still, Capital One's Spark Cash Select puts up a good fight. With no foreign transaction fees and 5% back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel, it could be the better fit for some business owners. To learn more, read our full review of the Ink Business Unlimited and our full review of the Capital One Spark Cash Select. Apply here: Ink Business Unlimited Credit Card Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Select For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: Better stays and bigger value with the Marriott Bonvoy American Express cards
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.50
Better stays and bigger value with the Marriott Bonvoy American Express cards There's a reason TPG awarded Marriott Bonvoy with Best Hotel Loyalty Program for two years and counting. Actually, there are several. With more than 30 brands and over 9,000 properties across the globe, you'll find exactly what you are looking for when you stay with Marriott, whether it's a luxury stay, a budget-friendly getaway or anything in between. When it comes to earning and redeeming points, Marriott Bonvoy's structure is surprisingly simple and lucrative. Marriott Bonvoy members earn up to 10 points per dollar spent on qualifying charges at hotels participating in Marriott Bonvoy, which can be redeemed for hotel stays and room upgrades, or transferred to more than 38 airline programs. And the perks you can get at Marriott Bonvoy's elite status tiers — like bonus points, space-available room upgrades, early check-in and late checkout (subject to availability) — add comfort and value to your stays when booked with a qualifying rate at hotels that participate in Marriott Bonvoy. Room upgrades are subject to availability upon check-in and only available to Gold and Platinum Elite members. Right now, you can earn even more points and get on the fast track to elite status with elevated welcome offers on two Marriott Bonvoy® American Express® Cards. These offers end Sept. 30, 2026, so let's take a look at how to choose the right card for your travel style. A top-tier card with premium benefits The Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card is the most premium card in the lineup, offering benefits that enhance not only your Marriott stays but also your everyday life. New Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant cardholders can earn 150,000 bonus points and a $250 statement credit after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Offer ends Sept. 30. The Bonvoy Brilliant card has a $650 annual fee (see rates and fees), but when you combine the Bonvoy Brilliant's annual free night award (available upon annual card renewal, certain hotels have resort fees), which can be redeemed for up to 85,000 points per night at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels, and the annual $300 Brilliant Dining Credit (up to $25 in monthly statement credits for eligible dining purchases worldwide each calendar year), it's easy to get outsize value from the card before you even dip into the other benefits. Cardholders also get complimentary Marriott Bonvoy® Platinum Elite status, which includes benefits such as 50% bonus points on stays at participating brands, lounge access, room upgrades and late checkout. These benefits are subject to availability and apply only when a stay is booked at a qualifying rate at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels. You can earn up to a staggering 21 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels on the card: 6 points for paying with the Bonvoy Brilliant card, up to 10 points for being a Marriott Bonvoy member and up to 5x points from Marriott Bonvoy on eligible hotel purchases with the 50% bonus points on stays benefit for Platinum Elite members. And with no foreign transaction fees (see rates and fees) and either a $120 statement credit for Global Entry or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck every four years, frequent travelers will reach for this card again and again. Whether you are a Marriott loyalist or only stay a few times each year, the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant card's complimentary Platinum Elite status, annual free night award (certain hotels have resort fees) and bonus points earning potential make it easy to take full advantage of its suite of benefits. And, if you apply by Sept. 30, you can earn 150,000 bonus points to use toward your next dream vacation. High earning potential for Marriott loyalists If you are looking for a lower annual fee or don't fancy yourself a frequent traveler, but still want to enjoy the benefits of elite status, the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card is a solid mid-tier option. The Bonvoy Bevy card has a $250 annual fee (see rates and fees), and new cardholders can earn 125,000 bonus points and a $150 statement credit after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Offer ends Sept. 30. Bonvoy Bevy cardholders get perks like a welcome gift of points when you stay at participating Marriott brands, automatic complimentary Marriott Bonvoy® Gold Elite status, complimentary room upgrades (subject to availability upon check-in) and a 2 p.m. late checkout (based on availability, when the stay is booked with a qualifying rate at hotels that participate in Marriott Bonvoy). You can also earn up to 18.5 Marriott Bonvoy points for every $1 spent on eligible purchases at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels: 6 points for paying with the Bonvoy Bevy card, up to 10 points for being a Marriott Bonvoy member and up to 2.5 points with the 25% Bonus Points on Stays benefit for Gold Elite members. When you combine the bonus points you can earn on stays, plus the Bonvoy Bevy's 125,000-point welcome offer, you'll be on your way to points-fueled vacations in no time. Bottom line No matter which card you choose, it's clear that a Marriott Bonvoy American Express card is the upgrade your next trip needs. Learn more about the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant American Express Card and the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy American Express Card before these elevated offers end on Sept. 30. For rates and fees of the American Express Bonvoy Bevy, click here. Terms apply to all offer and benefit mentions.

item.title: Which AAdvantage card is right for you? Here are 3 options you should consider
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.17
Which AAdvantage card is right for you? Here are 3 options you should consider Editor's Note If you're considering a cobranded card with American Airlines, it's important to pick the right option for you. Each choice offers a different annual fee, its own set of perks and distinct earning rates. Among Citi's five AAdvantage cards, you may be struggling to decide which is the best for you. Here are my thoughts on which of the three most popular AAdvantage cards is the right fit for you, depending on how dedicated you are to American Airlines and how frequently you travel. Citi / AAdvantage credit cards: Key details Before diving deeper into each card individually, let's go through a quick refresher of their basic details. | Card | Welcome offer | Standout benefit | Annual fee | |---|---|---|---| | | Earn 50,000 bonus miles after spending $2,500 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. | | $0 introductory annual fee, then $99 | | | Earn 60,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. | | $350 | | | For a limited time, earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. | | $695 | The information for the Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Platinum Select: For those who fly AA occasionally If you only fly AA a couple of times each year, I recommend the AAdvantage Platinum Select. Its $0 introductory annual fee for the first year (then $99) means you can test having a cobranded card in your wallet without committing to an annual fee up front. While you won't get any lounge passes or statement credits with merchants, you may not need the Platinum Select to play that role if you already hold a premium travel rewards card. That doesn't mean the Platinum Select slacks on perks, though. You'll get your first checked bag free on domestic American Airlines flights, saving you at least $45 each way. Plus, you'll receive priority boarding on all American Airlines flights. More often than not, I find passengers on my flights are forced to check their carry-ons after the plane runs out of overhead space. With priority boarding, the odds of that happening to you are lower. And unlike some other cobranded cards, you don't need to book your flight with your Platinum Select card to enjoy these perks. To learn more, check out our full review of the AAdvantage Platinum Select. Globe: For those who fly AA often If you fly with American Airlines at least once a quarter but aren't a fully committed loyalist, the AAdvantage Globe is a solid choice. While it comes with a $350 price tag, it offers a roster of perks to offset the cost. Some of these benefits are four annual Admirals Club passes, up to $100 back as statement credits for inflight purchases, up to $100 Splurge statement credit for eligible brands (exclusions apply) and a companion certificate for eligible flights after each account anniversary (worth $99 plus taxes and fees). If you're able to use the companion certificate each year and take advantage of the lounge passes, you should get outsize value out of your annual fee without even having to touch the card's statement credits. That said, if you only fly with American a couple of times each year, you may have to put in more effort than it's worth to get sufficient value out of the Globe. In that case, I recommend considering a general travel rewards card instead. To learn more, check out our full review of the AAdvantage Globe. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Globe Executive: For those very loyal to AA As AAdvantage's top-tier credit card, the AAdvantage Executive is oriented toward those who fly American Airlines exclusively or very frequently. And it carries an annual fee to match: $695. Given that this annual fee is as high as it is, it requires careful consideration to ensure it fits your budget. While the Globe offers four Admirals Club passes each year, the Executive offers an Admirals Club membership. Given that a full Admirals Club membership costs a whopping up to $1,400 for new members, if you visit an Admirals Club several times a year, this benefit alone makes the annual fee worth it. While an Admirals Club membership is this card's standout benefit, it also offers travel credits, hotel and car rental elite status, and priority AA travel perks to help justify its annual fee. It's also worth noting that if you fly Alaska Airlines frequently in addition to AA, this card can be a great fit for you. To learn more, check out our full review of the AAdvantage Executive. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive Is it worth having multiple AAdvantage cards? The main appeal of an AAdvantage card is access to American Airlines–specific perks, such as priority boarding, a free checked bag and, on premium cards, Admirals Club access. For most travelers, one well-chosen AAdvantage card is enough to unlock meaningful value. That's especially true if you're not trying to stack statement credits, chase multiple welcome bonuses or fully commit to the AAdvantage ecosystem. Instead of holding multiple AAdvantage cards, many travelers will get more flexibility by pairing the AAdvantage card that best fits their travel habits with a premium travel rewards card. A premium card can complement your AA perks with broader lounge access, transferable rewards and additional statement credits. That said, if you do want to build out a wallet with more than one AAdvantage card, it's important to keep Citi's welcome bonus eligibility rules in mind so you're able to secure the strongest offers available. Alternatively, you could look at a Citi Strata card to earn flexible ThankYou Rewards points that can be transferred to a variety of airline partners, giving you more options beyond AA. Bottom line AAdvantage is one of the most popular airline loyalty programs, and it's a favorite among many of my colleagues here at TPG. If you're considering a Citi / AAdvantage card, you'll find several strong options designed to suit different types of American Airlines flyers. When choosing the right card, it's important to think realistically about how often you fly American Airlines and whether you're comfortable prioritizing AA over other carriers. It's also worth considering how frequently you travel through airports with Admirals Club locations, as lounge access can dramatically affect the overall value of certain cards. Pick the AAdvantage card that aligns with your travel habits, and you'll unlock perks that can meaningfully improve your experience — from smoother boarding to valuable savings and, in some cases, comfortable lounge access along the way. Related: How to choose an airline credit card

item.title: Aeroplan card's best-ever offer: Earn up to 115,000 bonus points
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.02
Aeroplan card's best-ever offer: Earn up to 115,000 bonus points Editor's Note The Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card (see rates and fees) recently underwent a major refresh, adding several valuable travel perks while increasing its annual fee from $95 to $195. New and existing cardmembers now receive automatic Aeroplan 25K status with no spending requirement, 15% savings on eligible Air Canada award flights and up to $100 in annual Air Canada statement credits. For a limited time, new cardmembers can also earn up to 115,000 bonus Aeroplan points: 75,000 bonus points after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, plus an additional 40,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first 12 months from account opening. Here's what to know about the card's best-ever offer. Aeroplan card welcome offer The $195-per-year Aeroplan card is currently offering new cardholders its best-ever welcome offer. New cardholders can earn up to 115,000 bonus Aeroplan points: 75,000 bonus Aeroplan points after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, plus an additional 40,000 bonus Aeroplan points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first 12 months from account opening. TPG's September 2026 valuations place Aeroplan points at 1.5 cents apiece, making this welcome offer worth $1,725. However, earning the full bonus requires $20,000 in spending during the first year, so before applying, consider whether that spending requirement fits naturally into your budget. Keep in mind that this card is affected by Chase's 5/24 rule, which means you will likely not be approved if you have opened five or more personal cards in the past 24 months, regardless of which issuer they're from. If you are eligible, check out our ideas for quickly meeting a minimum spending requirement, including prepaying insurance, rent or taxes to earn the entire welcome offer. Related: Air Canada's Aeroplan program: The ultimate guide to earning and redeeming points Aeroplan card earning rates Beyond its welcome offer, the Aeroplan card earns bonus points across several travel and everyday spending categories: - UPDATED: Up to 5 points per dollar spent on eligible Air Canada purchases — 3 points from the card plus 2 additional points from Air Canada when traveling as an Aeroplan 25K member - NEW: 3 points per dollar on travel purchases other than Air Canada - 3 points per dollar spent at grocery stores and dining (through Dec. 31, 2026; these categories will earn 2 points per dollar starting Jan. 1, 2027) - UPDATED: 2 points per dollar on gas station purchases - 1 point per dollar spent on other purchases The addition of 3 points per dollar on general travel is particularly useful, but the card will become less rewarding for dining and grocery purchases when those categories drop from 3 points per dollar to 2 points per dollar in 2027. Related: Maximizing credit cards to become points-rich without spending a ton Aeroplan card key benefits Beyond the points that you can earn, the Aeroplan card also offers several benefits that can be particularly valuable for frequent Air Canada travelers: - Automatic Aeroplan 25K elite status with no spending requirement, and all the benefits that come with this status - 15% savings on eligible flights booked with Aeroplan points - Up to $100 in annual Air Canada statement credits, split into two up to $50 semiannual credits - First free checked bag for cardmembers and up to eight travel companions traveling on the same reservation (travel must originate on an Air Canada flight) - No foreign transaction fees - Travel protections, such as auto rental insurance, baggage delay insurance, roadside assistance, trip cancellation and interruption insurance and trip delay reimbursement - Up to $120 statement credit for a Global Entry, TSA PreCheck or Nexus application every four years The card's Air Canada statement credits can help offset the $195 annual fee, while the 15% award discount can provide additional value for cardmembers who regularly redeem Aeroplan points for eligible itineraries that include Air Canada flights. Additionally, cardholders can continue to earn a 500-point bonus for every $2,000 spent on the card per calendar month, up to 1,500 bonus points per month, through Dec. 31, 2026. This benefit will be discontinued starting Jan. 1, 2027. Related: Credit card perks and benefits you should be using this month Bottom line The refreshed Aeroplan card is a strong option for frequent Air Canada travelers, especially with automatic 25K status, 15% savings on eligible award flights and up to $100 in annual Air Canada statement credits. The $195 annual fee is a big jump from the previous $95, but the current best-ever welcome offer of up to 115,000 points sweetens the deal. Aeroplan points can unlock flights on Air Canada and its extensive network of airline partners, including United Airlines. If you already have a use in mind for Aeroplan points and can comfortably meet the $20,000 spending requirement for the full bonus, now could be a good time to apply. To learn more, read our full review of the Aeroplan card. Apply here: Aeroplan card
